---
name: concept-space-additions-map
description: Adding new rule families to arbitrary_exception_rule_prior barely moves MAP ll (~-1067); which additions were tried
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3 (2026-10-30), adding one new rule family (own Dirichlet weight) to the incumbent arbitrary_exception_rule_prior (MAP ll -1067.0):
- offset residue classes r mod k, k=3..6: -1066.7 (best; submitted as offset_progression_concepts, iter_3/candidate_0)
- same with k up to 12 or 25: -1067.2, weight -> 0
- multiples of 13..50: -1067.8; digit-sum = s: -1067.2 (weight 0.08); odd multiples/2-adic: -1067.2; decade blocks: -1067.3
After 69,9,39,21 the model still predicts 0.61 "yes" for 19 (observed 0/5), even with offset progressions in the space.
**Why:** the concept space is not the bottleneck. Remaining residuals are scattered single cells with n=5.
**How to apply:** don't spend another round on concept-space additions. See [[powers-of-2-37-misfit]].

Round 4 (2026-10-30), iter_4/candidate_1: a rule-vs-range prior log-odds that grows linearly with the number of examples (rule_noticing_grows_with_examples), added to parity_within_range_concepts. MAP ll -1063.98 for both models; the slope ≈ 0.03. The set size does not change how readily people think of a rule, so don't retry this.
---
name: example-recall-subset-mixture
description: Round-4 memory-limit model (independent recall of each example, mixture over recalled subsets) on parity_within_range base; linear-space matvec trick makes it fast
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 4 (2026-10-30), example_recall_limited_concepts: each example recalled w.p. r (Beta(4,1.5)), p_yes = mixture over non-empty recalled subsets of the parity_within_range_concepts learner.
First attempt (iter_4/candidate_2) REJECTED as too slow: 84 ms logp+grad; production is 4 chains × (3000 tune + 4000 draws) at target_accept 0.99 within 30 min.
Repair (candidate_2_repair_1): compute in linear space — per state exp(ll - max) likelihoods summed per interval size, and per (cell, subset slot) the same sums restricted to target-containing concepts; then evidence and "contains" are just matvecs with the prior vector. 2 ms logp+grad (logp identical to old). Also declared SAMPLER_SETTINGS draws/tune 1000, target_accept 0.95. Full 4-chain fit 92 s, 0 divergences, recall ≈ 0.987, novelty-pool RMSE vs recall→1 ≈ 0.005.
**Why:** the gradient of a large row gather (AdvancedIncSubtensor1) dominated the cost; the matvec form removes it.
**How to apply:** use the same linear-space matvec layout for any concept-mixture model with per-set states; see [[incumbent-residual-diagnostics]].
---
name: experiment2-data-structure
description: experiment2 responses = 10 participants x 450 trials, 2 stimulus orders; PPC keeps row order; shown-example targets get only 62% yes
metadata:
  type: project
---
experiment2 (2026-10-30): responses.csv is 4500 rows = 10 participants × 450 (participant = cumsum(trial_index==0)), only 2 distinct stimulus sequences; 119 sets. The PPC harness (src/critique/ppc.py) copies the CSV and overwrites only `rating`, so row-order/participant/lag statistics are valid.
Raw observations: when the target is one of the shown examples (85 trials) the yes rate is only 0.62 — the lapse-free incumbent predicts ~1, so a lapse/guessing term looks likely to be needed. Session late-minus-early yes rate -0.06; participant yes-rate SD 0.087.
**Why:** iter_0 critique statistics were built on this structure.
**How to apply:** check the iter_0 ppc_results.json for which of these turned out significant; see [[round4-null-refinements]] for the experiment1 data layout.

name: incumbent-residual-diagnostics
description: Round-3 tests on arbitrary_exception_rule_prior (quick 300-draw NUTS lppd, incumbent -1068.1); which single changes help
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3 (2026-10-30), iter_3/candidate_3. Incumbent is well calibrated (rescaling rule/range shares gains <1 nat); worst sets are 4,66,78,96, 31,3,1,15, 23,35,95,83 (parity+magnitude patterns).
- Helped: "odd/even within a range" concept kind (third Dirichlet kind weight ≈0.07, same Erlang width prior): lppd -1065.1 (+3). Submitted as parity_within_range_concepts.

- Too slow: per-interval (5050-column) likelihood with an exponent on range evidence — >10 min for 600 draws; keep per-size aggregation in prepare_observed.
**Why:** avoids re-running these next round.
**How to apply:** build on parity-within-range if it was admitted; see [[powers-of-2-37-misfit]].

name: multiples-within-range
description: Round-4 repair (iter_4/candidate_4_repair_1): "multiples of m within a range" kind on parity_within_range base — weight 0.04, ll -1.4 vs incumbent
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 4 (2026-10-30), iter_4/candidate_4_repair_1, multiples_within_range_concepts: incumbent parity_within_range_concepts + a 4th kind "multiples of m (3..9,11,12) within a range", same Erlang width prior. **How to apply:** don't build more rule∩range conjunction kinds. Check novelty against sibling candidates in the same round before submitting.

name: parity-range-width-variants
description: Round-4 MAP tests on parity_within_range_concepts (MAP ll -1064.0): gamma width +1.7, separate parity-range width scale 0
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 4 (2026-10-30), iter_4/candidate_4. Incumbent parity_within_range_concepts MAP ll -1064.0 (sigma≈30, kind weights .47/.47/.06).
- Gamma width prior (shape, mean inferred) grafted on: -1062.2 (shape≈4.1, mean≈56). Submitted as gamma_width_parity_range_concepts.
- Separate Erlang scale for parity ranges vs plain ranges: -1064.2 (no gain).
**Why:** saves re-running these.
**How to apply:** width-prior tweaks are close to exhausted; see [[incumbent-residual-diagnostics]], [[concept-space-additions-map]].

Round 4, iter_4/candidate_5 was rejected as an exact duplicate of gamma_width_parity_range_concepts (candidate_3 had already submitted that graft). name: powers-of-2-37-misfit
description: Incumbent family-prior models over-predict "yes" to 37 after powers-of-2 sets; splitting exception rules into own family gains ~8 nats MAP
metadata:
  type: project
---
In experiment1 (round 2, 2026-10-30), the incumbent erlang_interval_family_prior_concepts gave target 37 p≈0.35 after powers-of-2 sets; observed 0/25. Putting "powers of 2, not 32"/"or 37" in their own family raised MAP ll from -1075.5 to -1067.0 (candidate iter_2/candidate_5, arbitrary_exception_rule_prior).
Things that did NOT help at MAP: rule∩range conjunction concepts (-0.8), linear-in-log-odds response (+2 for 2 params), changing fixed noise ALPHA from 0.9.
Remaining misfit: predictions in the 0.2–0.4 band run ~0.07 too high (wide-range concepts extending beyond the examples).
**Why:** saves re-running diagnostics next round.
**How to apply:** start refinements from these residuals; see [[incumbent-residual-diagnostics]].
Round 3 (2026-10-30): gamma-width prior + exception family (iter_3/candidate_5, gamma_width_exception_family_concepts) MAP ll -1064.6 vs incumbent -1067.0 (+1 param; shape≈4.6, mean width≈53). Largest remaining per-set deviance: 4,66,78,96 (~-30, flat ~0.37 predicted, noisy data), 31,3,1,15, 23,35,95,83.

Round 3 (2026-10-30): generative "next-output probability relative to max, ^sensitivity" judgment on the incumbent learner gave MAP ll -1123 (vs -1067) — membership-probability reporting is clearly better; don't retry size-principle-on-target readouts.

Round 4 (2026-10-30): iter_4/candidate_3 = gamma_width_parity_range_concepts (incumbent parity_within_range_concepts + gamma width prior from gamma_width_exception_family_concepts). Smoke-fit ll -1066.8 (100 draws); passes check in ~75 s.

name: round4-null-refinements
description: Round-4 quick-NUTS tests on parity_within_range_concepts (lppd -1065.0) — sampling shape, multiples prior, fuzzy edges all fail
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 4 (2026-10-30), iter_4/candidate_0, quick NUTS (2x300) lppd; best model parity_within_range_concepts = -1065.0. Calibration by set size, in/out of span, parity, distance, p-bin is near perfect.
- Center-weighted ("representative") sampling within ranges, exp(-k u^2): k=2 -1075, k=5 -1112, k=-2 (edge-weighted) -1080. Uniform is best.
- Multiples-of-k prior ∝ k^beta: beta≈0, -1065.0 (no gain).
- Fuzzy range edges at readout exp(-d/λ): λ=1 -1065.4, λ=3 -1067.1.
- Data = 5 participants × 450 identical trials (rows in blocks of 450; trial_index resets), but no participant_id column and design rows lack trial_index — person-level models not safe.
- find_MAP on these Dirichlet models gave bogus ll (-1390); use quick NUTS instead.
**Why:** saves re-testing. **How to apply:** see [[incumbent-residual-diagnostics]], [[concept-space-additions-map]].
- Doubling/tripling chains (a·2^k, a odd ≥3; a·3^k), own family: -1066.1 (tie, weight ≈0.04). Submitted as doubling_chain_concepts (iter_4/candidate_0); current data have no chain-like sets, so the disagreement is on untested sets like 5,10,20.

p=-1

45 rules and all intervals of 1..100 (size principle, examples from the concept

L^(k-1) exp(-L k / mu) over interval width with shape k and mean mu inferred.
The single change (grafted from arbitrary_exception_rule_prior): the two
gerrymandered rules -- "powers of 2, not 32" and "powers of 2, or 37" -- form

import pytensor.tensor as pt
from scipy.special import logsumexp

ALPHA = 0.9
NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)

    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules


_RULES = rule_concepts()
RULE_NAMES, RULES = list(_RULES), list(_RULES.values())
N_RULES = len(RULES)
INTERVALS = [list(range(m, n + 1)) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]
MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES + INTERVALS], dtype="float64")

        return 0
    if name == "primes":

    if name.startswith("powers"):

    if name.startswith("multiples"):
